items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: the same Fletcher Henderson arrangements that first gained him national attention

ctx.x: Oh, gee, well I haven’t really played with that many big bands. I was lucky enough, I will sound like I’m dropping a name, but I’m real proud to drop this name, I was lucky enough to play with Benny Goodman for the last seven months of his life. And he had just put a big band back together again. He continued playing all through the 60s and 70s and 80s, but mostly with smaller groups. He’d have maybe a trumpet and sax and a rhythm section you know. But toward the end of his life he decided to put together a big…

international prominence, and in a way his life kind of went full circle because he went right back to the same music, the same Fletcher Henderson arrangements that first gained him national attention. So it was maybe the most exciting seven months in my life. And I’ve described it as being, you know people ask what it’s like playing for Benny Goodman and it’s equal measures of excitement and terror.
Describe that for us. Kind of give us a hypothetical.
